text:
jay (support): customer ops -> multiple tenants reporting a sudden spike in 5xx for hosted inference since ~13:02 UTC. some calls getting 502/504, others time out. ticket snippets: 'text-gen returned 502', 'stream aborted mid-token'.

alex (oncall): looking. can you paste a sample request + time window? any common model or region? :rotating_light:

jay (support): pasted below — all in us-west-2, mixed models but mostly gpt-open-16k variants. sample curl they used: ```curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-open-16k","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate``` returned HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway and connection reset.

metrics-bot: alert: 5xx_rate increased from 0.2% -> 6.8% across prod-hosted between 12:58–13:05 UTC. error breakdown: 65% 502 gateway, 25% 504 upstream timeout, 10% 500 internal. top impacted route: /v1/generate.

deploy-bot: recent rollout: rl-2026-03-15-09 by maria at 12:59 UTC. change: feature flag enable_continuous_batching=true for hosted inference canary (10% traffic).

maria (eng-runtime): I pushed a canary that increases batching window and raises default batch_size cap to 128 for some model shapes. initial unit tests ok but I'm seeing increased mem pressure on a subset of hosts. logs show repeated `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `runtime: out of memory` in a few containers.

luke (sre): looking at host logs — several pods OOMKilled in the canary pool 13:00–13:03. LB started routing around but gateway started returning 502 when remaining pods momentarily saturated.

alex (oncall): that matches the timing. this looks like a bad canary config (batching increase) causing memory blowouts -> 5xx surge. plan: revert flag to false for canary, roll back rl-2026-03-15-09, and scale up temporarily if needed. can someone start rollback now?

maria (eng-runtime): initiating rollback to previous config (enable_continuous_batching=false) for canary and redeploying the pool. command I'm running: ```redwoodctl rollout rollback rl-2026-03-15-09 --to-revision rl-2026-03-15-08```

jay (support): meanwhile customers asking for repro steps. I captured a failing trace: ```HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
server: envoy
content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream connection reset by peer","request_id":"req_abc123"}```

maria (eng-runtime): also seeing this in pod logs: ```runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000 bytes
fatal error: runtime: out of memory
--- FAIL: Serve (0.12s)``` which indicates the batching spike pushed memory beyond limits on smaller instance types in the canary pool.

luke (sre): quick mitigation: scaling canary pool nodes by +50% and evicting the smallest instance types. I'll trigger an autoscale override and taint small nodes out of service. running: ```k scale --replicas=30 ds/canary-inference --namespace=prod-hosted```

deploy-bot: rollback started for rl-2026-03-15-09 at 13:08 UTC. target revision rl-2026-03-15-08.

metrics-bot: post-action snapshot: 13:10 UTC — 5xx rate fell from 6.8% -> 1.9% within 2 minutes of rollback. still above baseline but trending down.

alex (oncall): good. please keep scaling override until we confirm stability. maria, let's run a canary in a smaller slice with memory-probed config and limits. add memory headroom to batch controller and add an OOM alert.

maria (eng-runtime): agreed. tests to add: 1) run synthetic load with large batch windows on t3-small equivalents, 2) run canary at 1% traffic for 30m with memory monitoring enabled, 3) add guardrail in code to cap batch_size if free_mem < threshold.

sara (product): customers hit by this — we should send an incident note and proactive outreach to high-traffic tenants. can support draft a brief? I'll help.

jay (support): drafting now. include timeline, impact, mitigation, and next steps.

luke (sre): followups: 1) add rollout pre-check to simulate memory effect for batch config, 2) block batch_size > 64 on canary by default, 3) add tighter health-check routing so LB doesn't route when pod starts failing to accept connections.

alex (oncall): creating incident ticket and assign postmortem to eng-runtime + SRE. owner: maria + luke. please add repro artifacts and the failing pod logs to the ticket.

maria (eng-runtime): uploaded logs and the failing heap traces to the incident. I'll open a PR for the guardrail and reduced default batch_size.

metrics-bot: 13:15 UTC — 5xx back to 0.6%, within normal variance. marking alert as acknowledged.

alex (oncall): closing this thread for active mitigation; leave comments if anything else pops. postmortem due EOD tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
